device.type: DVB-T HD PVR receiver with two tuners (2011)
device.board: MC6245-M3606-VER1.0 (elektroda topic "Cabletech URZ0086. Potrzebny wsad pamięci")
device.demod: unknown (under the tuner's shield, Gutek's review); the firmware has NIM_COFDM_0 / NIM_COFDM_1: two tuners

source.author: Lechpol (Cabletech / Kruger&Matz), mirrored by Gutek

simulator.note: With its board's chip ID 0x3603 (device.chipId, 2026-10-13) it boots and draws: the bootloader reads the flash with the quad I/O read 0xEB, the SEE's video drivers decode the boot logo -- video_m36.py's video engine and video output models are wired onto the SEE core and interrupt the core whose controller has the line enabled -- and the SEE's OSD driver draws the first-install wizard in Polish ("Witaj": Region Poland, Język polski, Tryb wyświetlania 576i, Tryb proporcji 4:3LB, Tak) within 230 M instructions.  Until the model read the stream buffer's address right (its bits 24..27 sit in the register's bits 27..30) the engine consumed every bit it was given, and in some runs the SEE stopped at its bit-buffer accounting's assertion (0x860BC008) around 90-100 M instructions.  Before (as 0x3602): As the M3602 family (2026-10-12): the bootloader starts the SEE co-processor -- chips/see.py runs its boot code at 0xA1E8D688, which copies the SEE's program into place, sets the started flag and parks the SEE -- prints "success!" and starts the application, which starts the SEE's program at 0xA6000200 on the second core (see.SeeCore) and attaches its drivers through 63 remote calls the SEE answers (and 18 of the SEE's, which the main CPU answers), printing its register dump; no GE command within 60 M instructions.  Further on (2026-10-13) it creates its OSD region (CLUT8, 568 x 512 at 76, 32) and draws 5 GE commands by ~85 M, when two things stop it: (1) the SEE's MPEG decoder read its VLD bit offset (0xB8004228) back with bits 8..25 cleared by the M3801's status-word model and stopped at its read-pointer assertion -- fixed (ChipFamily.ve_status); (2) the application's USB host open (0x801B77CC) asserts (SDBBP) on a controller without a register base: its attach (0x801B7300) gives one only on chip 0x3101 or on 0x3603 (0xB8032000 / 0xB8032400), while sys_ic_get_usb_num says 1 port on any other chip -- so the real board's M3606 reads 0x3603, like the X110TS's.  Under 0x3603, though, its bootloader's chunk check reads all-zero headers ("malloc size: 0", "CRC bad4") although the flash window holds the image: its flash driver's 0x3603 path (the S3602F's, sflash at 0xB802E000; the CPU / DRAM clocks from the strap pins differ) is not modelled yet.

desc: Cabletech URZ0086 firmware V1.1.1, the manufacturer's USB update image as Gutek's site mirrors it (urz0086_v111.rar); the archive also holds the update instructions (the box's menu: Narzędzia / Aktualizacja oprogramowania przez USB, the file chosen under "Allcode") and the change list.

Despite the .abs name it is a complete flash image: the ALi chunk chain from offset 0 -- bootloader 0x000000 (DVBS2---0.1.0, 2011-04-14), HDCPKey 0x01FE00 (Demo s3602, 2011-04-14), maincode 0x020000 (M3606 2Tuner, 2011-11-15), seecode 0x140000 (M3606 SEE, 2011-11-15), Radioback 0x240000 (1.0.0, 2011-04-14), countryband 0x250000 (1.0.0, 2011-04-14), userdb 0x26FF80 (1.0.0, 2011-11-15); the maincode's CRC-32/MPEG-2 is intact.  Banners in its LZMA streams: Libcore version 5.0.0@SDK4.0ba.5.0_20110425; Libcore version 1.1.5a@SDK_20100524.

The bootloader chunk's version reads "DVBS2---0.1.0" (ALi's project name) although the box is DVB-T; the maincode is "M3606 2Tuner".  Forum users program these .abs files directly into the flash (renamed .bin): they are complete flash images.

Change list (lista_zmian.txt, Polish): URZ0086_V1.0.7.abs / - soft bazowy / URZ0086_v1.1.0.abs / - Poprawiono j. polski w menu, / - Dodano znaczniki nagrywania w liście kanałów. / URZ0086_v1.1.1.abs / przywrócono odtwarzanie plików .flac

Gutek's review of the URZ0083 and URZ0086 (https://www.gutek.com.pl/tunery_cabletech_urz0083_urz0086_recenzja.htm): the URZ0083 is built on the ALi M3601E with an ALi M3100 demodulator and 64 MB DDR2, the URZ0086 on the ALi M3606 with 128 MB DDR2.  The simulator runs them as the M3602 family (chips/m3602.py).

Its second tuner's I2C bus is bit-banged (2026-10-13): the application drives GPIO 44 (SCL) and 43 (SDA) open-drain and sends the same MaxLinear sequences there (0x60: 0xFF 0x00, 0x02 0x01, reads through the 0xFB prefix) as to the first tuner on the hardware master SCB0 -- the board's two front ends (device.gpioI2c, gpio_i2c.py; no tuner model answers on either yet).
